acceptance: A change that removes a history-bearing comment group (the commentaudit check rule) with no matching labelled section added under docs/history/code-comments is refused by the commit gate, naming the file, line and the command that records it (red first)
A change whose removed history groups all appear in a section it adds passes, and a move (the group reappears whole elsewhere in the change) needs no section
The rule is commentaudit.RemovedHistoryAcrossDiff, the same one `commentaudit history` uses, with no second copy
fix: Beside refuseAddedComments, add a refusal that computes RemovedHistoryAcrossDiff over the staged change and requires each removed group to be present in a docs/history/code-comments page section the same change adds.
source: console, 2026-09-30, architecture review of the comment history archive (finding 3)
summary: The operator's rule (2026-09-30) is that the history comments carried must be recorded and stored. `commentaudit history` records it into docs/history/code-comments, but only the comment-reduction rounds run it; no gate does. The tree still holds about 3,338 history-bearing comment lines under the widened rule, so a loop lane or console change that deletes such code lands with no archive entry, and git's diff is again the only record.
title: Refuse a commit that removes history-bearing comments without recording them in the history archive
